result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

result.rule: When the description states that a decision is communicated to an affected participant and then describes actions conditional on that decision: Model the communication so it occurs on every outcome path for which it is stated, including paths that skip the conditional action; do not omit an outcome-specific communication when the description requires it.
When the description states that a participant selects or specifies inputs before a subsequent process action: Model that selection or specification as an explicit task before the dependent action.

When the description says a participant performs a concrete action that initiates the process, rather than merely identifying an event that triggers it: Model the initiating action as a task after the start event and before the subsequent activity; do not represent the action only as a start event.

When the description says an activity may occur in addition to the main sequence: Model the activity on an optional path, using a decision gateway to determine whether it occurs, and rejoin the main sequence afterward.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. When the description identifies actions or outcomes at distinct stages of a process: Label each BPMN element to reflect the action or outcome described at that stage; do not substitute a different action, a later-stage action, or an unsupported outcome.
